mission: Torin walks down the ridgeline toward the valley. The group watches. Each silence has distinct texture: Ben (failed to stop this pattern once before), Sera (was the person whose agency was overridden), Kael (spent his life being stopped), Desh (breaks the silence first with operational pragmatism). Sera's line lands: 'I was the one they sealed. I cannot seal another.'
why_now: The turn's physical enactment. If the group physically restrains Torin, the book's thesis collapses. The scene is the refusal to repeat the pattern the book has spent twenty chapters condemning.
conflict: The impossible choice. Stop Torin by force — and repeat Gavran. Let him go — and lose the group's strongest member to a dangerous plan. Each character's silence carries the ghost of their own wound. Sera's is the one that says the book's argument out loud.
turning_point: Sera, barely above a whisper: 'I was the one they sealed. I cannot seal another.' Ben nods. The group has made a choice without voting.
opening_hook: Torin walks down the ridgeline toward the valley. His stride is steady. His Force presence trails behind him — lighter than it's been since he woke up.
closing_hook: Sera's voice, barely above a whisper: 'I was the one they sealed. I cannot seal another.' Ben nods. He understands. And now he must find another way.
emotional_trajectory: Helpless watching -> the agony of principled inaction -> Sera's devastating clarity

stakes.personal: Each character confronting their deepest wound through the choice to let Torin go
stakes.interpersonal: The group diminished — their strongest member gone
stakes.external: Torin heading toward the Scar to become the new seal

setting: Veranthos — camp, watching Torin walk away down the ridgeline
sensory_details: Torin's receding figure — steady, unhurried; the wrongness parting around him as he walks into it; Sera's face holding grief on iron; Kael's hands loose at his sides — the posture of someone refusing to grab; Desh's voice as the first sound after too much silence: 'So. What now?'
action_beats: Torin turns and walks down the ridgeline toward the valley — stride steady, Force presence trailing behind him
Sera stands motionless as Torin descends, her hands clenched at her sides — refusing to seal another
Desh breaks the silence: 'So. What now?' — the first sound after too long
promises_paid: The Jacen parallel recognized and pattern broken (PP07)
notes: The book's emotional centre. Ben has seen this before; this time he chooses differently. He does not chase, does not fight, does not force. Each silence is authored: Ben's held breath, Sera's iron composure, Kael's refusal-to-grab, Desh's breaking of the silence. Anti-pattern: do not physically restrain Torin — the scene's thesis is that refusal is the choice. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, name the Jacen pattern as resolved in interiority. Sera's line is the book's moral architecture spoken aloud for the first time; it does the naming. One line, one nod, one question from Desh, and the chapter moves.
